**Item No. 2: Review of Member Feedback and Finalisation of Scope of Work**

The Chairperson opened the discussion by recapping the summary of suggestions tabled at the previous meeting. A total of 23 suggestion slips had been received, with the highest priority being waterproofing and seepage-related works (9 suggestions), followed by gymnasium upgradation (5), washroom renovation near the pool (4), painting and flooring (3), and furniture repair (2).

Mrs. Meera Joshi reported that she had spoken further with residents of the top floor flats in Buildings A and B. The seepage in the bedrooms of flats 1201 and 1202 in Building A had worsened after the recent rains in February. She stated that the residents were anxious for the waterproofing work to commence at the earliest, even if it meant that some other items of work would need to be deferred.

Mr. Nitin Agarwal said that he had also received verbal feedback from members using the gymnasium. Several members had enquired whether the new treadmills could be ordered soon, as the existing machines were frequently out of order. He suggested that the committee could consider ordering the gymnasium equipment separately so that the delivery timeline is not linked to the main civil works.

Mr. Prakash Deshmukh, who had been co-opted for his engineering background, advised the committee that the waterproofing work on the terrace should not be delayed beyond the onset of the monsoon. He stated that the ideal window for such work is between March and May, as the terrace needs to be completely dry for the application of the waterproofing membrane. He recommended that the waterproofing contract be awarded immediately and the work commenced by mid-March.

After discussion, the committee unanimously agreed on the following revised scope of work:

1. Waterproofing of the terrace and external walls – **Highest priority; to commence first.**
2. Repair and repainting of interior walls and ceilings in the lobby, corridors, and common areas – **To be carried out after waterproofing is completed.**
3. Replacement of damaged vitrified tiles in the lobby and corridors – **To be clubbed with the painting work.**
4. Repair and reupholstery of furniture in the lounge area – **To be carried out in parallel.**

8. Renovation of the washrooms near the pool – **Deferred to the next phase, subject to availability of funds. The committee noted the feedback but decided that the current budget would not permit this item without compromising on the core waterproofing and seepage works.**

The decision to defer the washroom renovation was recorded. Mrs. Meera Joshi noted that the residents who had requested this work would need to be informed of the committee's decision, and she volunteered to draft a notice for circulation.

---

**2. Review of Waterproofing Work – Terrace and External Walls**

Mr. Jadhav presented a detailed update on the waterproofing work. The work on the terrace of Wing A has been completed. The contractor has applied the final coat of the elastomeric membrane on 15th May 2024. A water ponding test was conducted on 17th May 2024, and the terrace was kept under water for 48 hours. No leakage was reported from the flats below. The committee appreciated the contractor for adhering to the testing protocol.

Regarding Wing B, the first two coats of the primer have been applied. Mr. Deshmukh inspected the site on 18th May 2024 and observed that the contractor is not following the correct curing process. The primer coat applied on 16th May was not allowed to cure for the required 24 hours before the second coat was applied. The contractor was instructed to stop further work immediately, and the supervisor was asked to redo the affected area. The contractor representative, Mr. Pawar, accepted the lapse and confirmed that the rework will be completed by 22nd May 2024. The committee decided that the contractor will bear the cost of the material and labour for the rework, and this will be deducted from the final bill.

**Decision 1:** The committee resolved to issue a formal warning letter to M/s. Shree Balaji Constructions for not adhering to the specified curing time. The letter will be drafted by the Secretary and sent by 22nd May 2024. The chairperson will also conduct an unannounced site inspection on 23rd May 2024 to verify the rework.

---

**3. Status of Interior Wall and Ceiling Painting**

The painting work for the lobby and corridors commenced on 6th May 2024 as scheduled. The contractor has completed the priming of all internal walls and ceilings. The first coat of paint has been applied in the lobby area. The committee noted that the colour shades, Warm Ivory (4342) for the lobby and Soft Grey (4451) for the corridors, are matching the approved samples.

However, Mr. Iyer raised a concern regarding the quality of the putty application in the corridor near the lift lobby on the 3rd floor. He observed that the putty is not smooth and has visible brush marks. Mr. Jadhav explained that the putty is still drying and will be sanded before the final coat. The committee instructed the contractor to ensure that the walls are properly sanded and cleaned before the final coat is applied. The work is expected to be completed by 28th May 2024, and the committee will do a final inspection on 30th May 2024.

**2. Monsoon Preparedness Review – Status of Pending Items**

The chairperson called for a review of the decisions taken at the previous meetings. The supervisor, Mr. Pawar, was present for this item. He reported the following:

- **Western side storm water drain:** The desilting work was completed on 12th June 2024. The drain is now clear. The chairperson asked the supervisor to take a photograph of the cleared drain and share it with the committee for records.
- **Pruning of trees:** The gardener completed pruning on 13th June 2024. The branches near the parking area and children's play zone have been cut. The committee noted that the gardener has been asked to collect and dispose of the cut branches, which he did on 14th June 2024.

The number has been shared on the society WhatsApp group and a circular was put up on all three notice boards. Mrs. Deshpande confirmed that the helpline has received 14 calls so far. The CRC had presented the roof inspection findings at the previous meeting. The members were informed that the roof has multiple cracks and the waterproofing layer has aged. The committee had agreed that the roof repair is a separate urgent matter.

Mr. Shinde informed the committee that the waterproofing contractor, M/s. AquaSeal, has provided a quotation for the roof repair. The quotation was circulated along with the agenda. The total estimated cost is ₹4,85,000, which includes:

- Removal of the existing broken waterproofing layer
- Repair of the concrete screed where the cracks are deep
- Application of a new polyurethane-based waterproofing membrane
- Provision of a 5-year workmanship warranty

The committee discussed the quotation in detail. Mr. Kharat pointed out that the quotation does not include GST, which would be extra. The contractor has confirmed that GST will be charged at the prevailing rate of 18%. The total cost with GST would be ₹5,72,300.
